author: DailyMail
title: The Largest Known Early World Map May Have Pointed to Noah's Ark for Nearly 440 Years
text:
The Planisphere, created by Italian cartographer Urbano Monte in 1587, contains a small depiction of Noah's Ark resting on the mountains of Ararat, sparking fascination due to its alignment with the mysterious Durupınar site.
The largest known early world map, created in 1587 by Italian nobleman and cartographer Urbano Monte , may have pointed to the resting place of Noah's Ark for nearly 440 years.
The Planisphere, measuring nearly 10 feet across when fully assembled, is packed with elaborate illustrations of continents, mythical creatures, and unexplored lands. A small depiction of Noah's Ark resting on the mountains of Ararat, the same region believed to hide the legendary vessel, is hidden within the map. The striking detail has sparked fascination because the Bible states in Genesis 8:4 that the Ark came to rest on the 'mountains of Ararat.
' Researchers have investigated the Durupınar site near Mount Ararat, Turkey, hoping to determine whether the formation is a natural geological structure or the remains of the biblical Ark. A team recently claimed to have identified hidden chambers and tunnel-like spaces beneath the earth using ground-penetrating radar
